messages:
raj: Heads-up — seeing a sustained p99 spike (~2x) on shared-gpu-pool-B starting ~09:12 UTC. Throughput dropped ~20%. Appears correlated with several long-history requests from tenant:acme-realtime.

michelle: saw that on dashboards, grabbed a flamegraph — looks like kernel switching around KV cache misses.

eva: @raj can you paste the runtime logs? I want to check kernel select decisions + batch coalescing.

raj: paste from runtime logs (truncated):
```
2026-02-14T09:12:05Z runtime INFO kernel_selector: chosen=quant_fast kernel=matmul_q8_asm seq_len=256 batch=8
2026-02-14T09:12:05Z runtime WARN kv_cache: miss_rate=0.28 tenant=acme-realtime route=/v1/generate
2026-02-14T09:12:06Z runtime INFO kernel_selector: autoswitch candidate=quant_fast->quant_fallback reason=mem_peak delta=320MB
2026-02-14T09:12:06Z runtime INFO kernel_switch: applied=quant_fallback latency_penalty=0.9ms
2026-02-14T09:12:07Z runtime INFO batching: coalesced_batches=3 pending=12
2026-02-14T09:12:07Z runtime INFO kv_cache: miss_rate=0.67 tenant=acme-realtime
2026-02-14T09:12:08Z runtime ERROR perf: tail_p99=450ms p50=38ms
```

toa: interesting — kv cache miss rate jumped before the kernel autoswitch. Could be long contexts evicting shared KV for others.

sam: I pulled a perf trace from the node — shows recurring context swaps and a few 100ms stalls in memcpy on the same GPU. Suspect noisy tenant is doing many long seq requests which break the KV locality.

runtime-bot: autoscaler event: pool-B node-17 marked as degraded at 09:13:22 UTC (latency above SLO). Routed new requests to pool-B nodes 3/8.

raj: quick repro summary: single tenant flashes a burst of seq_len~2048 requests (batching disabled by client), causes KV working set to exceed L2 capacity -> kernel_selector tries quant_fast (memory optimized) but misses in tiled GEMM path -> falls back to quant_fallback which is slower for this shape. Combined with increased memcpy due to cache thrash = p99 spike.

eva: can we mitigate short-term? Options: 1) per-tenant concurrent request limit, 2) pin large-context jobs to dedicated pool, 3) force kernel selection policy to prefer stability over peak perf during high miss_rate.

michelle: operationally I throttled tenant:acme-realtime at the edge (reduced concurrency 70% for 10m) which brought p99 back to baseline. Leaving throttle for now until we have a plan. :white_check_mark:

toa: follow-ups:
- run kernel selector sim with synthetic seq_len=1024/2048 mix and verify fallback thresholds (ACTION: eva)
- add kv_cache_eviction metric per-tenant to make thrash visible in console (ACTION: sam)
- consider a short-term routing rule to isolate >1024 seq jobs into a "large-context" subpool (ACTION: runtime infra)
- file a perf regression if we confirm quant_fallback got slower vs last release (ACTION: raj)

raj: opened perf ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RWI-5123 — attached flamegraphs and kernel traces.

infra-bot: deploy tracker: no infra deploys during incident window. GPU driver versions consistent across pool-B.

eva: quick note on kernel selector heuristics — current logic weights (mem_pressure 0.7, latency 0.2, fallback_penalty 0.1). We could add a stability bonus when kv_cache_miss_rate > 0.4. I will run A/B sim and post results.

sam: logged metric request for kv_cache_evictions and tenant-local memcpy stalls. Also adding a dashboard tile for per-tenant mem_watermark.

michelle: thanks all. Keeping throttle in place for 30m. If tests show we can change kernel selection safely we'll do a canary rollout next week.

raj: closing loop here for now. Will coordinate with @eva and @sam on root cause and action items. If other nodes show same pattern, we'll escalate.

eva: quick attachments I will add to the ticket: sample RPC traces, kernel timings, and the selector decision matrix.

michelle: :thumbsup:
